research_topics.topic_text:
Research overseas graduate exchange and short-term visiting scholar/student programs in the United States for students in New Media Technology, Journalism & Communication, Public Opinion Research, and Computational Social Science.

Focus on top institutions (e.g., University of Southern California Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism, University of Pennsylvania Annenberg School for Communication, Stanford University, Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism / Data Journalism, New York University Steinhardt/Carter Institute).

Examine:
1. Curriculum & Teaching Models: Interdisciplinary course structures, computational social science/data journalism/media tech seminars, hands-on lab projects, project-based evaluation, industry/lab collaborations.
2. Credit Transfer & Requirements: US credit system conversion rules, credit load for full-time exchange/visiting status, prerequisite requirements.
3. Academic Culture & Research Atmosphere: Seminar participation expectations, faculty office hours, lab cultures, research assistant opportunities, academic integrity.
4. Financials, Visas & Language Requirements: Detailed cost structure (visiting tuition/program fees, living expenses in major US cities like LA/NYC/SF/Philadelphia), J-1 vs. F-1 visa regulations (DS-2019, Proof of Funding requirements, work authorization restrictions), language proficiency thresholds (TOEFL iBT scores, IELTS Academic scores, waiver rules).
5. Scholarships & Financial Aid: Visiting scholar grants, university exchange waivers, institutional financial aid for visiting/exchange graduate students.
6. Long-Term Value & Practical Strategies: Impact on academic development, joint publications, networking, and actionable strategies for classroom/cultural integration, mental health/stress management, and personal risk management in US urban university settings.

Research overseas graduate exchange and short-term visiting student/scholar programs in Europe—specifically focusing on the United Kingdom, Netherlands, and Germany—for students in New Media Technology, Journalism & Communication, Public Opinion Research, and Computational Social Science.

Focus on leading institutions:
- United Kingdom: London School of Economics and Political Science (Department of Media and Communications), King's College London (Department of Digital Humanities / Media), University of Amsterdam (ASCoR - Amsterdam School of Communication Research)
- Netherlands: University of Amsterdam (ASCoR / Communication Science), Erasmus University Rotterdam
- Germany: LMU Munich (Department of Media and Communication / Computational Social Science), Free University of Berlin (Institute for Media and Communication Studies)

Examine:
1. Curriculum & Teaching Models: ECTS (European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System) credit weights, modular course structures, interdisciplinary media and computational social science offerings, practical vs. theoretical orientation.
2. Credit Transfer & Requirements: How ECTS credits transfer back to non-European home institutions, typical ECTS semester loads (30 ECTS), eligibility criteria.
3. Academic Culture & Research Atmosphere: Self-directed learning, lecture/seminar structures, tutorial systems (UK), research institute access (e.g., ASCoR labs, German research groups).
4. Financials, Visas & Language Requirements: Estimated living expenses (London, Amsterdam, Munich/Berlin), tuition/fee structures for non-EU visiting/exchange students, visa regulations (UK Student Visa / CAS, Dutch Residence Permit / MVV, German Student Visa / Blocked Account - Sperrkonto), language requirements (IELTS, TOEFL iBT, English-taught program requirements, German language expectations if any).
5. Scholarships & Financial Aid: Erasmus+ mobility grants (where applicable for international exchange), DAAD (German Academic Exchange Service) grants, Dutch government/NL Scholarship, UK university visiting bursaries.
6. Long-Term Value & Practical Strategies: Academic networking in European media research networks (e.g., ECREA), publication opportunities, classroom integration strategies, cross-cultural adaptation, mental well-being, and health insurance/safety management.

Research overseas graduate exchange and short-term visiting student/scholar programs in Asia—specifically focusing on Singapore and Japan—for graduate students in New Media Technology, Journalism & Communication, Public Opinion Research, and Computational Social Science.

Focus on top institutions:
- Singapore: National University of Singapore (NUS - Department of Communications and New Media / Centre for Trusted Internet and Community), Nanyang Technological University (NTU - Wee Kim Wee School of Communication and Information)
- Japan: University of Tokyo (Graduate School of Interdisciplinary Information Studies - III/GSII), Waseda University (Graduate School of Political Science / Journalism), Keio University (Media Design / Policy and Media)

Examine:
1. Curriculum & Teaching Models: Modular/course credit systems, English-taught graduate modules, computational social science/media tech tracks, hands-on lab work, project-based vs. thesis-focused models.
2. Credit Transfer & Requirements: Credit conversion systems, semester credit loads, home university transfer guidelines.
3. Academic Culture & Research Atmosphere: Lab system (Kenkyushitsu culture in Japan), hierarchical vs. collaborative dynamics, seminar dynamics, research lab expectations.
4. Financials, Visas & Language Requirements: Tuition and living costs (Singapore, Tokyo), visa processes (Singapore Student's Pass / STP, Japan Student Visa / Certificate of Eligibility - CoE), language requirements (TOEFL, IELTS for English programs; JLPT N1/N2 rules for Japanese programs or English-taught tracks).
5. Scholarships & Financial Aid: MEXT (Monbukagakusho) exchange scholarships, JASSO scholarships for short-term study in Japan, Singapore University exchange subsidies/grants, ASEAN/international mobility funds.
6. Long-Term Value & Practical Strategies: Asian digital tech and media market exposure, academic networking (e.g., ICA Asia chapters), classroom integration strategies, cross-cultural adaptation in Asian academic settings, mental health resources, and safety/risk management.
